kitDescription: Cinderella is an Electric rocket-launcher Defender (Burst III, 40s cooldown) whose whole design converts a huge HP pool into attack power. Her rockets must be fully charged, but after the first full charge she gains +100% Charge Speed that only goes away when she reloads to full ammo, and every full-charge hit tacks on extra damage worth 136.6% of her ATK. At the start of battle — and again each time the team reaches Burst Stage 3 — she summons a decoy avatar holding 96% of her Max HP; while a decoy is up she accumulates 'Beautiful', +1.6% Max HP every 3 seconds up to 12 stacks (+19.2% once it caps around 36 seconds). Every Burst Stage 3 entry also gives her bonus ATK equal to 2.71% of her final Max HP for 10 seconds, so the larger her HP pool has grown, the harder everything she does hits. Her own burst fires ten sequential hits of 1365.92% ATK into random enemies, plus an extra 28.9% ATK hit multiplied by her current Beautiful stack count — meaning her nuke gets meaningfully stronger the later in the fight she casts it.

redAssertions: burst 'the sequential volley is sequential-flavored (feeds Sequential Attack Damage)' — the driver's consolidated 13659.2 instance carries no flavor field. THE ONE RED THAT IS A REAL FAITHFULNESS GAP (gotcha G2).
burst 'is TEN discrete 1365.92% hits, not one merged hit' — driver ships ONE consolidated flatDamage 13659.2 (same total; EV-equivalent vs a partless single boss).
burst 'burst-cast damage ... lands 10x per cast' (hits.length >= 10 x casts) — 1 damage instance per cast under consolidation.

S1b 'is chargeSpeedPct 100 with removeOnReload and NO time bound' — driver ships no chargeSpeedPct effect at all; the cadence is modeled by charFixes.magDumpRof (video-measured). DOCUMENTED_GAP, not a defect.
S1b 're-applies per shot and is stripped at reload (buffRemove cause reload)' — no chargeSpeedPct buffApply/buffRemove events exist under the mag-dump encoding.
S1b 'charge speed IS damage — it gates shots fired' — CF_CS_ZERO patches 0 effects, so the counterfactual is a no-op against the shipped file.
S2c 'is a self Max HP buff of 1.6, capped at 12 stacks, interval 3s, in skill2' — driver ships one smooth casterMaxHpPct 19.2 rampSec 36 filed under skill1; skill2 is [].
S2c 'stacks 1..12 in the event log and never exceeds the cap' — no discrete per-stack buffApply events under the smooth-ramp encoding.
S2c 'feeds her own S1a HP->ATK conversion' via CF_BEAUTIFUL_ZERO — patches 0 effects because the search is scoped to skill2 while the block lives in skill1.

fixture non-vacuity + attribution sanity — S5 placed onEvent on the CompOptions root instead of cfg, so its event log is empty. RECON_ERROR (harness-API misuse by the blind author), not a driver defect.

NOTE ON THE GREEN RE-RUN: the driver-reconciled adaptation (blind/cinderella.adapted.test.ts, 20 passed / 3 skipped) re-expressed the burst assertions behaviourally (total magnitude, FB-exemption, cast count) and thereby dropped the flavor assertion. That adaptation must NOT be read as clearing G2 — it removed the assertion that caught it.

skill1.kitLine: ATK ▲2.71% of final Max HP, 10 sec
skill1.driverSaid: skill1[0]: stageEnter{stage:3} -> self, buff atkOfMaxHpPct 2.71, durationSec 10.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 blind override byte-identical (stat, value, trigger, target, duration). S5's behavioural assertions (HP-scaling stat, 600-frame expiry, self scope, one grant per stage-3 entry) all pass against the driver unchanged.
skill1.formulaCheck: SSOT: atkOfMaxHpPct is the ATK-from-own-MaxHP conversion; liveMaxHp = static base + OWN-kit maxHpFlat only. Target self, and Beautiful is self-granted (casterIdx===self), so the Beautiful ramp legitimately feeds it and ally Max-HP grants are correctly excluded (cindy e3 rule).
skill1.explanation: Trigger identity is exactly right: stageEnter{3} fires on ANY team stage-3 entry (helm's as well as her own), not burstCast and not fullBurstEnter — the misread S2b ranked as most damaging. The grant's value grows across the fight as Beautiful accrues, as predicted. The one open question is not this encoding but whether her own SAME-CAST grant reaches her nuke — see gotcha G1, filed on burst line 1.

skill1.driverSaid: No chargeSpeedPct buff. charFixes.magDumpRof true + reloadFrames 120: one ~1.0s charge primes the mag, all 24 rockets autofire at datamined rate_of_fire 180, ~2.0s reload re-arms the prime. Sourced to an ammo-counter frame read (docs/probes/720-kit-audit/cindy solo neutral.MP4), owner-ruled, Fable pre-op APPROVED-WITH-REVISIONS, recorded in the note AND a dedicated caveat.
skill1.blindSaid: Both blinds (S5 assertions, S6 override) encode the literal prose form: chargeSpeedPct 100 on shotFired with removeOnReload and no durationSec. Three S5 assertions go RED on the missing buff.
skill1.formulaCheck: SSOT magDumpRof: 'one charge primes the mag, then the whole magazine autofires at datamine rate_of_fire without recharging, then reload-to-max re-arms the prime. Charge Speed shortens only the once-per-mag prime.' That is a direct restatement of the kit clause ('charge once, keep firing, lose it on reload-to-max'), reproduced as the measured cadence rather than as a chargeSpeedPct multiplier.
skill1.explanation: Mechanism substitution, not a drop: a direct measurement of the disputed quantity (shots/sec via ammo counter) outranks a literal prose reading of the mechanism, and the substitution is recorded with provenance. Driver test C2 pins it two ways — >300 pulls/180s and >2x the per-rocket-charge counterfactual, plus a ~20f median intra-mag gap that a charge cycle cannot produce. Residual to keep on file (already in the caveat): she now carries no chargeSpeedPct buff, so ally charge-speed support touches only the once-per-mag prime, and any consumer keyed on her having a Charge Speed buff sees nothing. n=1 recording — MEASURED, not datamined.

skill1.driverSaid: skill1[2]: shotFired -> enemy, flatDamage atkPct 136.6, no core, no noFb, crit-eligible by default.
skill1.blindSaid: S6 identical (adds a redundant explicit crit:true). S5's behavioural assertions — 136.6 magnitude, enemy target, no core, FB-eligible by landing timing — all pass against the driver unchanged.
skill1.formulaCheck: SSOT: flatDamage riders are critEligible by default, noRange is engine-forced, and FB participation is decided by landing timing (correctly NOT flagged noFb — it lands inside the FB window on in-FB pulls). Routed as a plain rider, not through the charge bucket, so no chargeDamagePct double-dip.
skill1.explanation: Fires once per pull — driver test asserts riders.length === shots.length exactly, so the rider count rides the mag-dump cadence and cannot silently under-fire. Trigger is shotFired where the prose says 'hitting'; against the single partless boss with RL splash these are equivalent, and the video recon at ~97.5s independently confirms 2 popups per pull (rocket + rider) reconciling to one ATK of 80,385.

skill2.driverSaid: Verbatim in unmodeled.skill2, plus a caveat stating the consequence: the v1 boss deals no damage, so full decoy uptime — and therefore unconditional Beautiful uptime from t=0 — is assumed.
skill2.blindSaid: Both blinds unmodeled it identically and both flagged the same load-bearing consequence (the presence-gate must resolve TRUE from battle start, else all Beautiful stacking silently zeroes).
skill2.formulaCheck: v1 has no avatar entity and no damage-taken model, so the summon has no offensive routing. Correctly NOT encoded as a shield or heal — either would spuriously fire teammates' shielded/on-recovery triggers (crown is in the fixture).
skill2.explanation: The unmodeled decoy is inert, but the 'decoy always present' premise it licenses is load-bearing for the entire Beautiful ramp; the driver states it explicitly rather than leaving it implicit. Correctly handled.

skill2.blindSaid: Both blinds unmodeled it; S2b notes the nearest-wrong model would be treating the re-summon as RESETTING Beautiful stacks, which nothing in the prose supports.
skill2.formulaCheck: Indistinguishable from the first decoy in a model with no avatar entity; a refresh path only.
skill2.explanation: Genuinely inert in v1 (the first decoy can never die against a damageless boss). The stack-reset misread is avoided — the driver's Beautiful ramp is monotone and never keyed to burst casts.

skill2.driverSaid: skill1[1] (filed in the skill1 array; skill2 is []): passive -> self, buff casterMaxHpPct 19.2, rampSec 36. 1.6 x 12 = 19.2; 3s x 12 = 36s.
skill2.blindSaid: S6 encodes the discrete form (targetMaxHpPct 1.6, maxStacks 12, interval 3s, in skill2); S5 asserts discrete per-stack events. Both derive the SAME 36s trajectory from the prose's own 3s x 12, so the two encodings agree on the curve and disagree only on step-vs-line.
skill2.formulaCheck: SSOT: casterMaxHpPct converts to a flat maxHpFlat grant at apply time; for a SELF target caster===target, so it feeds atkOfMaxHpPct exactly as the discrete form would. rampSec on a buff = linear min(1,(frame-startFrame)/rampFrames). Linear and discrete coincide exactly at every 3s boundary; inside a window the linear form over-credits by at most one stack (<=1.6% Max HP ~ <=1.4k ATK on ~170k, sub-1%). At her first cast (t~5.4s) it credits 2.88% where true stacks give 1.6%.
skill2.explanation: The offensive consumer chain is modeled correctly and is what matters: driver test C5 proves it two-sidedly — removing Beautiful drops the nuke's baseAtk, and an INSTANT ramp raises the first-cast baseAtk above the shipped gradual model, so the ramp is a property of the encoding, not a coincidence. Two low residuals, both documented and sub-1%: (a) linear interpolation instead of 12 discrete steps, (b) the block is filed in the skill1 array with skill2 left empty, which makes an empty skill2 slot look like a drop to anyone reading the file rather than the caveats. Neither is a gotcha; see G3.

burst.driverSaid: burst[0]: burstCast -> enemy, ONE consolidated flatDamage atkPct 13659.2, no flavor field. burstSnapshotsPreFb: false. Test C6 pins the exact 13659.2, one instance per cast, burst bucket, and fbMajorApplied never true.
burst.blindSaid: S6 emits TEN discrete flatDamage 1365.92 each with flavor:'sequential'; S5 asserts both the ten-hit shape and the sequential flavor (both RED vs the driver); S2b's spec names sequentialDamagePct (additive, diluted) and sequentialMultPct (own bucket) as the consumers. Neither blind could see burstSnapshotsPreFb — they were blind to the shipped file.
burst.formulaCheck: Magnitude and timing are right: 10 x 1365.92 = 13659.2 exactly, and against a partless single boss the 'random enemies' split is EV-equivalent, so consolidation is magnitude-neutral. TWO routing problems remain. (1) The SSOT damage chain carries a dedicated seqMult bucket, and the sequential flavor is what routes a packet into it — an unflavored instance is blind to all sequential support. (2) SSOT ordering: 'stageEnter blocks run before burstCast blocks at a cast', so with burstSnapshotsPreFb false her own same-cast atkOfMaxHpPct 2.71 IS live when the nuke resolves — while this file's own BURST TIMING record (e3 video + U10) states the nuke 'must lose ... the same-cast stage-3 ATK stack (burstSnapshotsPreFb flag)', and that paragraph is NOT in the 2026-07-21 rebuild's SUPERSEDES list.
burst.explanation: Fires once per cast, 6 casts over 180s, correctly FB-exempt by cast timing (fbMajorApplied never set) — the cadence and the FB half are clean. Two undocumented routing gaps sit on this line: G1 (same-cast snapshot contradicts the file's own recorded measurement; ~2x swing on baseAtk for ~45% of her fight damage; no test pins it) and G2 (missing sequential flavor). The consolidation ITSELF is documented and defensible; what is undocumented is what the consolidation discarded.

burst.driverSaid: burst[1]: burstCast -> enemy, flatDamage atkPct 346.8 with rampSec 36 (28.9 x 12 stacks, ramping with Beautiful).
burst.blindSaid: S6 EXACT convergence — 346.8 with rampSec 36, independently derived from the prose's own 3s x 12. S5's behavioural assertions (whole multiple of 28.9 capped at x12; a max-stack-authored mirror must carry a 24-48s ramp; an early cast must mirror fewer stacks) all pass against the driver unchanged.
burst.formulaCheck: SSOT: rampSec on a flatDamage is a per-battle-elapsed scale min(1, frame/round(rampSec x 60)) snapshotted at cast — exactly the semantics needed to reproduce the live stack count at cast time. 51.7 at t~5.4s -> 346.8 at t>=36s. Linear vs discrete over-credits the first cast (~52 vs a true 28.9), which is ~0.17% of that cast's total damage.
burst.explanation: This is the strongest convergence in the file: an independent blind, working from prose alone, produced the identical 346.8/rampSec-36 encoding. Driver test C7 discriminates properly — an instant-ramp mirror collapses every cast to 346.8, while the shipped model must produce a sub-346.8 first cast. Both blinds correctly flagged once-per-cast vs once-per-sequential-hit as measurement-gated (popup counting on a recorded burst); the driver models once per cast and that remains an open, recorded ⚑ rather than a defect.

gotchas.summary: Shipped burstSnapshotsPreFb:false lets her nuke snapshot her OWN same-cast stage-3 ATK conversion — the direct opposite of what this file's own e3-video record says must happen, on a flag worth roughly a 2x baseAtk swing across ~45% of her fight damage, with no test pinning either behaviour.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Activates when entering Burst Stage 3 ... ATK ▲ 2.71% of the skill user's final Max HP for 10 sec.' SSOT ordering: 'stageEnter blocks run before burstCast blocks at a cast' — so with the flag false the conversion is live when the nuke resolves. The override note's BURST TIMING paragraph (e3 video + U10) states the contrary as a measured finding: 'her nuke resolves PRE-full-burst and PRE-same-frame-stage-buffs ... with rockets fixed, the nuke must lose the FB x1.5 and the same-cast stage-3 ATK stack (burstSnapshotsPreFb flag)' — and that paragraph is NOT covered by the 2026-07-21 rebuild's 'SUPERSEDES below' list (which names only the charge-speed +45 ramp, the ~1.2s reload / ~315 pulls, and the TWIN-INSTANCE FIX). The driver's own PASSING C1 assertion is the proof of shipped behaviour: nuke baseAtk > 1.5x the atkPct counterfactual is only reachable if the HP-scaled grant is live at cast, and helm's earlier stage-3 grant (10s duration, ~20s apart) has lapsed by her cast. Neither blind could see this — they never saw the flag or the note. Magnitude context: normals ~390 pulls x ~265% vs 6 casts x ~14006% puts ~45% of her damage on this packet.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Do NOT pick a value to fit the board. Resolve the record: re-read ONE nuke popup from docs/probes/u8 e3 (cindy focus) — the two models differ by ~2x in baseAtk on the same cast, so a single popup settles it outright (and the file already reports early/late FB proc values 633.7k/667.0k from that footage, so the read is cheap). Then either (a) set burstSnapshotsPreFb true if the e3 reading holds, or (b) delete the stale BURST TIMING sentence and record the superseding measurement in the note + DECISIONS. Either way add a driver assertion that pins the nuke's baseAtk against her atkOfMaxHpPct state at cast, since nothing currently does. Working hypothesis for how it drifted (label it as such, unverified): when the engine adopted universal cast-instant FB exemption, the per-unit flag was cleared for its FB half and the same-cast stage-buff half went with it.

gotchas.summary: The consolidated 13659.2 nuke carries no sequential flavor, so the kit's 'Attacks sequentially for 10 time(s)' is unrouted and the packet is blind to the SSOT's seqMult bucket and to sequentialDamagePct / sequentialMultPct support.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Deals 1365.92% of final ATK as damage. Attacks sequentially for 10 time(s).' SSOT damage chain includes a dedicated seqMult bucket. S6's blind override tags all ten hits flavor:'sequential' and S5's flavor assertion is one of the ten REDs; S2b's spec names the exact consumers ('sequentialDamagePct (additive, diluted) and sequentialMultPct (own bucket) buffs from teammates apply'). The driver's note documents the arithmetic (1365.92 x 10 consolidated) but never the flavor decision, and the driver's C6 test asserts only the magnitude — so the attribute is dropped silently rather than deliberately. Board impact today is plausibly zero (seqMult defaults to 1 with no sequential buffer in the control comp) but I could not verify the graded-comp rosters, and 'inert' is a premise, not a given.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Add "flavor": "sequential" to the consolidated 13659.2 flatDamage. seqMult multiplies the whole packet, so 1 x 13659.2 flavored is arithmetically identical to 10 x 1365.92 flavored — the change is board-inert in any comp with no sequential buffer and correct in any comp that has one. If validate-overrides rejects flavor on a consolidated instance, either re-expand to ten flavored 1365.92 hits (also EV-identical vs the partless boss) or record the omission verbatim in the note as a deliberate, engine-limited skip. Before assuming zero board movement, check the actual graded-comp rosters for a sequential buffer rather than asserting inertness.

gotchas.summary: Beautiful is modeled as one smooth 36s linear ramp filed in the skill1 array rather than 12 discrete 3s steps in skill2 — sub-1% in effect and documented, but it leaves "skill2": [] in the shipped file and defeats any skill2-scoped audit or counterfactual.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: 'Activates every 3 sec when a decoy is present ... Max HP ▲ 1.6% continuously, stacks up to 12 times.' Driver: skill1[1] passive self casterMaxHpPct 19.2 rampSec 36. Linear and discrete coincide exactly at every 3s boundary; inside a window the linear form over-credits by at most one stack (<=1.6% Max HP, ~<=1.4k ATK on ~170k). At her first cast (t~5.4s) it credits 2.88% Max HP where the true stack count gives 1.6%, and the mirror rider likewise reads ~52 where discrete stacks give 28.9 — ~0.17% of that cast. Concretely demonstrated by S5's CF_BEAUTIFUL_ZERO counterfactual patching zero effects because it searched skill2.
gotchas.suggestedFix: No magnitude change warranted. Either move the block into the skill2 array (behaviourally inert for a stat buff — no slot-routed consequence — but it restores line-to-slot traceability and makes slot-scoped counterfactuals work), or add one line to the caveat saying the empty skill2 array is deliberate and pointing at skill1[1]. If step-vs-line ever matters, the discrete form is available: interval 3s / value 1.6 / maxStacks 12, which both blinds derived independently.

verdictRationale: Seven of eight kit lines are clean and the convergence is genuinely strong: the S1a HP->ATK conversion (stat, value, stageEnter{3} trigger, self scope, 10s) and the 346.8/rampSec-36 Beautiful mirror are BYTE-IDENTICAL to a blind re-derivation from prose alone, the 136.6% rider matches on magnitude, bucket, target and FB-by-timing, both decoy lines are unmodeled verbatim with their load-bearing consequence stated, and the three headline S5/S6 divergences (mag-dump vs chargeSpeedPct, smooth vs discrete Beautiful, consolidated vs ten-hit nuke) are all documented mechanism substitutions with provenance, not defects — the mag-dump in particular rests on a direct ammo-counter measurement of the disputed quantity, which outranks a literal prose reading of the cadence mechanism. The blocking finding is G1, and no blind agent could have caught it because both were blind to the shipped file: burstSnapshotsPreFb is false, which per the SSOT's stageEnter-before-burstCast ordering means her nuke DOES snapshot her own same-cast stage-3 ATK conversion, while this same override's BURST TIMING record — e3 video, not superseded by the 2026-07-21 rebuild's own SUPERSEDES list — states the nuke must LOSE that stack. The driver's passing C1 assertion is what proves shipped behaviour, so this is not a doc nit: the file's recorded measurement and its shipped flag disagree by roughly 2x on baseAtk for ~45% of her fight damage, and no test in either suite pins it. G2 is smaller but real and formula-confirmed: the consolidated nuke silently drops the sequential flavor the kit states and the SSOT has a seqMult bucket for; the fix is one field and is arithmetically inert wherever no sequential buffer exists. discriminationOk is false for coverage, not vacuity — every driver test that exists does fail under its named nearest-wrong model (C1 and C5 two-sidedly, C2 on cadence, C7 on ramp shape), but the two load-bearing properties behind G1 and G2 have no assertion at all, and note that the S5 'adapted' re-run went green precisely by re-expressing the flavor assertion away, so it must not be read as clearing G2. For GO: resolve G1 by re-reading one e3 nuke popup and then either flipping the flag or deleting the contradicted sentence (plus a test that pins the nuke's baseAtk against her live conversion at cast), and add the sequential flavor or record why it cannot be routed. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: every agent in this gauntlet including me is the same model family, so the shared prior most worth an independent look is the rampSec-36 linear-for-discrete substitution that all of us accepted without argument, and my read of burstSnapshotsPreFb's semantics — I inferred it from the note plus the driver's own passing assertion and could not read the engine source, so treat the flag's exact meaning as CONFIRMED-by-behaviour but PLAUSIBLE-by-name.
